description: Composite Super Swarm Evidence conformance vectors: a CMW collection per case, the recorded quote appraisal it is appraised against, and the SwarmClaims document every appraisal path must produce. Every case is replayed through every appraiser profile.

appraisers.name: recorded-offline
appraisers.description: The quote appraisal as the fixture records it, in the claim set's own spelling. It stands for the built-in offline appraiser: no fixture can carry a hardware signature over a request this repository invented, so the corpus holds the quote appraisal fixed and pins everything downstream of it.

appraisers.name: verifier-a
appraisers.description: A Verifier consumed as an EAT, through the production delegated appraiser: flat claim names, hex octets, its own issuer and signing key. It appraises the quote's signature and reports the registers; the image identity is derived locally from the RTMR0 event list, which no quote-only Verifier consumes.

outsideCoverage.reason: the attester's platform is outside the delegated path's coverage: a quote-only Verifier reports no image identity for it, and this corpus records a typed denial rather than a partial verdict

appraisers.name: verifier-b
appraisers.description: A second EAT-emitting Verifier, with nested claim names that share none of the first's, base64url registers, a base64 report data, a different issuer and a different signing key. Nothing about it is named in any implementation: it is configuration, and it must appraise this corpus into the same claim sets as the other two profiles.

cases.description: A membership root whose own TEE evidence is SEV-SNP, beside a TDX per-request quote. The delegated path delegates the per-request quote and appraises the membership root offline — the root's quote is part of the Super Swarm chain, not of the request — so a root the relying party's Verifier could not appraise changes nothing.
The two REQUIRED elements alone. No statement and no envelope, so no pod claim is reported — an absent claim was not established.
An envelope with nothing to pair: the node vouches that this quote answers this request, and no leader statement is carried, so `envelope_ok` is reported and the pod claims are not.

The envelope carries a GPU attestation token hash, which is the only thing that can set `gpu_attested`: the binding digest owns all 64 octets of the guest-chosen field, so a token hash cannot ride in the quote beside it.

The statement is signed by a leaf carrying no challenge extension — a chain from outside this PKI, or one issued before the authority recorded the enrolment. The appraisal still verifies the signature and still reports `statement_signer_binding: unknown`, because a policy that requires a hardware-bound signer has to be able to tell an unlabelled leaf from a claim this build did not produce. Nothing here is refused: what the binding is worth is the policy's decision.

The same parts under the CMW JSON collection of draft-ietf-rats-msg-wrap. The relying party runs one Verifier of its own choosing, and a collection carrying the same parts must appraise into the same claims whoever forwarded it.

The cluster space is not locked. That is a claim and not a denial: whether an unlocked space may receive a credential is the relying party's policy, and deciding it here would make the verdict unarguable.
The pod runs under the `privileged` Pod Security Standard. Reported, never judged — the five predicates live in the bank's policy module.
The registry answered, and the answer was `not one of ours`. `mrenclave_approved: false` is a statement a policy decides on, spelled differently from a claim nobody looked at.
The image is admitted by the relying party's own reference values rather than by a Super Protocol signature. It proves strictly less, and `mrenclave_source` is what says so.

An appraiser that appraises the quote and nothing else: it reports the registers and no image identity, because mrEnclave needs the RTMR0 event log replayed and normalised. Neither `mrenclave` nor `mrenclave_approved` may then appear — a policy reading `mrenclave_approved: false` would believe something was checked. The delegated profiles are the other half of the same point: handed the same quote, they replay the event list themselves and do report an identity.

verifier-a.note: the delegated path derives the image identity from the quote's own RTMR0 event list, so it reports one where a quote-only appraiser cannot

cases.description: The quote commits to another Target: the attester answered a different request, and nothing paired with it is relevant.
The quote commits to an earlier challenge's freshness element. A replayed quote is a quote about some other moment.
CEKpub was modified in flight: the quote commits to the key the attester was given, the relying party holds another, and the binding digest is what notices.

An appraiser that reads the guest-chosen field and will not say which field it read. On the Azure nested form the raw REPORT_DATA is the paravisor's, so a comparison against an unnamed field proves nothing.

verifier-a.note: the delegated path reads the guest-chosen field out of the quote itself and always names which field that was, so it cannot be the appraiser this case is about

cases.description: The envelope's `subject_hash` is some other public key's: the node vouched for a request that is not this one.
The envelope answers an earlier challenge, while the quote answers this one.
The envelope names another Vault target than the one being appraised — the draft's foreign additional-authenticated-data case, in this profile's spelling.
The envelope is signed by a node certificate of another cloud, under a root nobody pinned, and the membership element does not carry it.

The attester substitution the envelope exists to catch: a sound statement about a locked neighbour, attached to a quote taken over this requester's own key. Every other check passes, and only the envelope's `statement_hash` contradicts the pairing.
The statement is signed outside the pinned PKI. A leader's signature is only worth the chain behind it.
The membership chain validates — to a root of another cloud. The relying party pinned one anchor, and the system trust store is never consulted.
A statement with no envelope binding it to this request. It is the substitution shape itself, and not one of the three collections the profile pins.

expect.reasonContains: carries a statement and no envelope binding it to this request

cases.description: A GPU token hash inside an envelope the named certificate did not sign. The appraisal denies, so `gpu_attested` is never set — a token hash beside an envelope that did not verify vouches for nothing.

The RTMR0 event list the quote carries does not replay to the quote's own RTMR0, so no image identity can be derived from it. The appraiser reports a failure to reach an answer, which is a denial and not an unapproved image — and both paths reach it from the evidence rather than from a recorded verdict.
The signed objects are older than the relying party accepts. Both carry an `issued_at`, and the envelope is the one checked first, so that is where the window the caller configured refuses.
